# 04 · control/style-transfer

**Workflow:** [`stability/stability-04-style-transfer.json`](../stability/stability-04-style-transfer.json)

---

Two images in: a **composition** to keep and a **look** to apply. The only endpoint of the four with more than one dial, and the closest thing in the Stability API to what you would do locally with IPAdapter.

## The two inputs

- `init_image` — the newest file in `directory`. This is the composition being preserved.
- `style_image` — the newest file in `stability/style-refs/`. This is the look being applied.

Both are required. Getting them the wrong way round produces a plausible-looking image that is exactly backwards, and it is an easy mistake to make because neither slot complains.

## The three dials

This graph sweeps `composition_fidelity`, because it is the one you will actually reach for. The other two are pinned; move them once you can see what this one does.

- **`composition_fidelity`** (swept: 0.5 / 0.8 / 0.95) — how hard the init image's arrangement is held. **This is the dial to raise when structure drifts.** At 0.5 the composition is a starting point; at 0.95 it barely moves.
- **`style_strength`** (pinned 1.0) — how much of the reference's look lands. Lower it when the style overwhelms the subject.
- **`change_strength`** (pinned 0.9) — how far from the init image the result may travel *at all*, before either of the other two apply. Think of it as the outer bound. Drop it to ~0.5 for a restrained pass.

They interact: high `composition_fidelity` with low `change_strength` gives you something very close to the original, and there is a point past which you are paying for a copy.

## Where this sits against the other three

Structure holds arrangement but takes its look from the prompt. This holds arrangement and takes its look from a *picture*. When you have an approved card whose style you want spread across the deck, this is the endpoint — and it is what the deck cascade's anchor plates are ultimately for.

## Chaining these four

They all share one convention, and that is the whole mechanism — there is no workflow-calls-a-workflow in ComfyUI, so a folder is the join:

```
stability/in/              drop your sources here
stability/out/sketch/      <- 01 writes here
stability/out/structure/   <- 02
stability/out/style/       <- 03
stability/out/transfer/    <- 04
```

Every one of these graphs reads **the newest image** in its `directory` (`sort_by = modified`, `descending`, `limit = 1`). So to feed one endpoint's output into another, change this graph's `directory` to that graph's output folder and run it. Structure reading `stability/out/sketch` is a two-step chain; nothing else needs rewiring.

The filename carries through: `Load Images From Directory` emits `filenames`, which is wired to the save node's `label`, so `the-fool.png` stays `the-fool.png` at every stage and you can always tell which source a result came from. `overwrite` is off, so a second run lands as `the-fool_1.png` rather than destroying the first — and "newest by modified" still picks it up.

Each result gets a sidecar JSON with the prompt and settings that made it.

## Cost

Each of the three nodes below is **one paid call**, so a run is three. That is the point of a study graph — you are buying the comparison, not the image. **Ctrl+B** any of them to drop it from the run once you know which end of the dial you care about; bypass passes the input straight through and costs nothing.

Seeds are fixed at **7**. Stability treats seed 0 as "pick a random one", which would make the three results incomparable and stop any of them being cached. With the seed pinned, the dial is the only thing that differs between them.
